newsitem.title: UK: Insurers to be global buyers in 1997 -analysts.
newsitem.headline: Insurers to be global buyers in 1997 -analysts.

text.p: Aegon's acquisition of Providian Corp's insurance operations is part of a trend towards the creation of larger insurance groups spanning the globe, analysts said on Monday.
"There's been a steady stream of acquisitions and I see no reason why this trend should abate in the short term," said Robin Mitra, continental European insurance analyst at Merrill Lynch.
"Wherever you go, virtually everyone wants to grow in life insurance," said Mitra, adding that insurers' growth plans included developing Asian economies as well as established markets.

Aegon's $3.5 billion buy ends an active year in the insurance sector, which has seen the mergers of Royal and Sun Alliance in the UK and Axa and UAP in France, as well as considerable consolidation among reinsurers.
Apart from opportunities to cut costs, takeover activity among insurers is being be spurred by several other forces, analysts said.
Firstly, the demographic trends in OECD countries mean that more people are living longer with more disposable income. This is creating a growing market for life insurance savings products.
Secondly, there is a perception that the market for life, health and associated products may grow as the trend towards reducing state provision in many countries gathers pace.

Thirdly, many insurers are keen to expand their life operations in the belief that they represent a more stable flow of profits than non-life insurance, which is subject to the vagaries of weather and nature.
Analysts noted that the Providian deal, which is the largest to date in the U.S. life sector, represented a sound investment for Aegon.
Aegon itself was bullish in its statement, saying that it expected the Providian acquisition could increase earnings by five percent in 1998.
Aegon chairman Kees Storm told an analysts' telephone conference that other parties had been interested in Providian, although he did not know their identities.
Many insurers have stated their intention to expand and a number are sitting on the sidelines with large war-chests waiting for the right opportunity.
Analysts said Dutch insurer ING is looking to expand through acquisition, also in the U.S., while Aegon has said it has money for further acquisitions.

Australia's AMP said earlier this month it had A$5.0 billion to spend in the UK or U.S., markets on which South Africa's Donald Gordon, via his TransAtlantic Holdings Plc, is also focusing his attention.
In the UK, which is already undergoing a slow but steady consolidation in the life sector, Prudential Corp Plc is another known predator biding its time.

"There will be plenty more happening in insurance of a cross border nature in the next year or so," said one London based insurance analyst. adding that the probable move to a single European currency was one driving force.

"A lot of deals are being considered in anticipation of a single European currency, which will make cross border selling of insurance in Europe easier, although it won't solve all the problems," he added.
